This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing-
Interlocutory Application, This Day, The Court
Delivered The Following:
 -3-
 Mfa No. 101905 of 2016
 Judgment

Challenging judgment and award dated 23.01.2013, passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and Fast Track Court, Koppal, in MVC No.628/2010, this appeal is filed by claimant for Maheboob vs Manjunath on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127130851/
2 enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts as stated are that on 20.05.2010, claimant was riding bicycle by side of Kataraki road,
when a water tanker tractor bearing registration no.KA-37/8844, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed to bicycle causing accident.
In accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to District Government Hospital.

Thereafter, treated at SDM, Hospital,
Dharwad.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
3. Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against driver, owner and insurer of vehicle.
4. On service of notice, driver did not enter appearance.
He was placed ex-parte.
Only insurer and owner opposed claim petition on all counts.
5. Thereafter, tribunal framed issues, recorded evidence of claimant's father as PW1, eye witness as PW2 and Dr.H.Ramakrishna S/o Hanumanthappa, as PW3.
Exhibits P1 to P16 were marked.
In rebuttal, insurer got marked Exhibits R1 to R4 by consent.

6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of water-tanker tractor by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.1,22,000/- with interest at rate of 6% per annum.
7.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, claimant is in appeal.
8. Shri M. Amaregouda, learned counsel for appellant submits that claimant was a minor, aged 13 years and sustained grievous injuries to his left thigh.
Claimant sustained compound fracture of left femur with degloving injury of skin.

As per Ex.P12-disability certificate issued by PW3- Dr.H.Ramakrishna, claimant had sustained 20% disability to whole body due to loss of muscle and Ostio-arthritic changers at left thigh and knee joint.

It was submitted that though tribunal considered 20% disability and notional annual income of claimant at Rs.15,000/-, it awarded inadequate compensation towards future loss of earning at Rs.60,000/-.

On overall consideration,
award was inadequate and sought enhancement.
9. On other hand, Shri Nagaraj C.Kolloori, learned counsel for respondent-insurer submitted that claimant was a minor.

Considering disability assessed and taking into account that PW3-Doctor had not treated claimant, even loss of earning capacity were to be assessed below 10%, then claimant would be entitled for lump-sum compensation as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another reported in AIR 2014 Supreme Court 736.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another reported in AIR 2014 Supreme Court 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, award of tribunal would be justified.

10. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award and records.
Maheboob vs Manjunath on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127130851/
3
11. From above submission, occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle, issuance of policy and its validity as on date of accident are not in dispute.
Tribunal assessed compensation and held insurer is liable to pay same.
Insurer has not preferred any appeal.
Therefore, liability of insurer to pay compensation is also not in dispute.

Since, only claimant is in appeal, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
12.

Insofar as disability, claimant has produced wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills,
prescriptions and disability certificate marked as Exhibits P3 and P8 to 12 respectively.
Claimant has also examined Dr.H.Ramakrishna as PW3.
On perusal of said evidence, tribunal has considered disability at 20%.
Taking into account submission of learned counsel for insurer that assessment by doctor, who did not treat claimant would suffer from over assessment.
Considering nature of injuries and disability sustained, even if there is some moderation considered, disability sustained by claimant would be above 10%.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled to compensation under 2 n d slab, as per Master Mallikarjun's case (supra).
13. Thus, claimant is awarded a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- for injuries sustained.

As per said decision,
apart from said compensation, claimant would be entitled to actual amount spent towards medical expenses and for loss of income of parents during period of treatment.
It is stated that claimant had taken inpatient treatment for a period of 40 days.
Accident occurred in year 2010.
There is no specific evidence regarding income of parents.
Notional income for year 2010 is Rs.5,500/-.

Therefore, claimant would be entitled for loss of income of parents for a period of two months i.e.,
Rs.11,000/- (Rs.5,500/- X 2).
Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.52,184/- towards medical expenses against bills produced.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled to said amount also.

14. Thus, total compensation would be:
"Rs.3,00,000/- + Rs.52,184/- + Rs.11,000/- = Rs.3,63,184/-."
Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.
15.

In result, I pass following:
ORDER a. Appeal is allowed in part.
b. Judgment and award dated 23.01.2013, passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and Fast Track Court, Koppal, in MVC No.628/2010 is modified.
c.
